Subject: Post-demo recap + operational next steps

Hi Samira / Michael —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we covered (short):
- Core win: reduce inference cost on your agent scoring pipeline by ~40% with prefix caching + batching.
- Deployment model: leaning Private (VPC) for data controls; Dedicated as fallback for initial throughput.
- Integrations: S3 ingestion + streaming via Redwood SDK; latency SLO target 200ms p95.

Asks / next steps:
1) Economic buyer confirmation — you mentioned Rajiv on the last call; can you confirm Rajiv (CFO) is the final signatory for contracts?
2) Procurement & legal timeline — ask procurement to share required contract terms / MSA redlines and target dates.
3) Security questionnaire owner — please confirm who on your side will own the SOC2 / data residency questionnaire (Michael? someone from infra?).
4) Technical scoping call — propose 60 minutes on Sep 22 with Ben Carter (CC'd) to walk integration points and retention/keys.
5) I attached a 1-page mutual action plan (stubbed) and an ROI one-pager; if useful I'll send a version with our recommended milestones and delivery owners.

Attachments: [Attachment: Novalabs_MutualActionPlan_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 38KB)], [Attachment: Novalabs_ROI_one-pager.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 24KB)]

If that looks right, can you: 1) confirm Rajiv and procurement contact, 2) confirm Sep 22 for scoping?

Thanks —
Olga

Sr. AE, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + operational next steps

Thanks, Olga — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Rajiv Patel (rajiv.patel@novalabs.com) is the economic buyer and will be the primary sign-off for any procurement > $250k. I'll loop him in once we have a clean timeline.
- Procurement contact: procurement@novalabs.com (team mailbox). Primary handler is Hannah Li (hannah.li@novalabs.com) — she'll own the MSA/PO timeline.
- Security owner: Michael Rhee (CC'd) will lead the SOC2 Q/A and will forward the questionnaire to our security team.

Next steps on our side:
- Sep 22 for technical scoping works for Ben and Michael — please send an invite.
- For procurement, Hannah will need a redline-ready MSA or a clean 1-2 pager of standard commercial terms. Any chance you can provide the MSA template + highlighted spots we should expect?
- ROI one-pager looks useful; can you include a short TCO comparison for 6/12 months focusing on token/instance cost and expected latency improvements?

We would also like a short internal talk track (2-3 bullets) for Rajiv to explain the financial case — if Marissa has a template that would be great.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Products, Novalabs
samira.khan@novalabs.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-09-14T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + asks from Novalabs (procurement + Rajiv)

Ben / Marissa — forwarding Samira's reply. Key asks: redline-ready MSA + TCO for 6/12 months + 2-3 bullet executive talk track for Rajiv.

Ben: please prepare a scoping checklist for Sep 22 that covers: data routing, retention/keys, KV cache behavior, and expected token throughput. Include any prerequisites for Private deployment (VPC peering, KMS).

Marissa: can you draft a 2-bullet exec talk track and update the ROI sheet with a clear monthly cost delta and a 12-month NPV line? I'll attach the updated MAP and send to procurement.

Also flag anything in the MSA we should expect legal to push back on (SLA, data residency, indemnity).

Thanks —
Olga
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-14T14:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + asks from Novalabs (procurement + Rajiv)

Quick technical notes for the scoping call: 

- Integration surface: S3 ingestion (batch) + streaming via websocket for real-time scoring. We should confirm whether they will use our SDK or host the model client.
- Retention / keys: If they require short-lived keys + customer-managed KMS, Private deployment will be easiest. We should confirm KMS provider and whether HSM is required.
- KV cache: recommend enabling prefix caching for cost sensitivity; we'll need sample sequence-length distribution ahead of the call.
- Capacity: initial pilot target 200 QPS for scoring (p50 latency target 80–120ms, p95 200ms). Need to size GPU pool; propose 2 x A10s for pilot.

I can put a short scoping doc together (2 pages) by EOD that we can share. Any commercial constraints we should call out so I can size correctly?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
